## jig v0.2.0-alpha.6

The legacy relay no longer posts into a server's own channels. A peer's relayed post into a
channel the receiving server orders is refused, so a channel reaches another server only by a
share (#398, fixes #357). Clients can also verify a server's render against more than one
text-block build, ready for the Unicode 18 switch in a later release (#403).

This is an alpha. Pre-1.0 releases make no wire, receipt or storage compatibility guarantee, and
jig has not had an external security audit yet (D27).

### Breaking: the legacy relay no longer posts into channels

- **A post a peer relays into a channel this server orders is refused** (#398, fixes #357),
  whether it names the channel by slug or by id. Share any channel that reaches peers only
  through the relay; until then, peers' posts to it are refused and logged.
  - The refusal is logged with the reason `relayed-into-sequenced-channel`: the first per peer
    and channel at warn, the rest at debug. Each is counted in
    `jig_federation_relayed_refused_total{reason="relayed-into-sequenced-channel"}`.
  - Writes a follower relays under a share's grant are not affected: they reach the owner by the
    contract, not the legacy relay.
  - After this, the legacy relay lands only a peer's `channel-create`, and only under
    `federation.naively_accept_peer_relayed_creates`, which is for tests only.
  - Peers on an earlier release still send every post; each is refused. A later release stops
    the sender relaying what peers will refuse.
- **New relayed posts no longer stall a shared channel.** A channel that already stalled at a
  post the old relay carried between same-named channels stays stalled, with no in-place repair
  yet; `deploy/README.md`, "A stalled carried channel", has what to do.

### Fixes

- **Federation catch-up no longer asks again for every post it refused** (#398). It now
  remembers the last block it dealt with from each peer, refused ones included, and resumes from
  there, stepping back 32 rows. A reconnect asks again for at most those 32, not every refusal
  since the last block that landed.
- **Clients verify renders from more than one text-block build** (#403). This release ships the
  next build (Unicode 18 normalization) for verification only. Servers still render with the
  current build, so nothing renders differently in this release.
  - The next build's component hash is
    `blake3:99593614ee82449902364ae342cc9d4d671e39c9da0c2d236394908e3c351fb8`. Operators who
    allow text-block by component hash can add it ahead of the release that switches servers to
    it.
  - That later release changes text normalization to Unicode 18. 68 code points newly assigned
    in Unicode 18 will normalize under NFKC; all other text renders as before. Clients on this
    release or later will keep verifying across that switch.

### Operators

- **Admission effort follows load** (#325, JEP-0008 rules 17-19). For servers that set
  `[auth.admission] unknown_dids = "proof-of-work"`, the work asked of a new key now rises
  during a flood of unknown keys and decays when it stops, between `min_effort` (default
  2^20, the old fixed price) and `max_effort` (default 2^24, at most 2^28). The controller is
  tuned by `controller_window_secs`, `controller_target` and `controller_start_effort`.
  `min_effort = 0` asks no work while the server is quiet. Relayed and bridged authors never
  move it. Proof-of-work admission stays off by default.
  - `pow_bits` still works for this release and means `min_effort = 2^pow_bits`; an unset
    `max_effort` rises to meet it. Setting both `pow_bits` and `min_effort` is a boot error.

### Dependencies

- **argon2 0.6 and chacha20poly1305 0.11** (#400), with aead 0.6 and cipher 0.5. Key files and
  sealed blobs written by earlier releases open unchanged; published vectors and a `.jigkey`
  file at the default KDF parameters check it. jig-core enables chacha20poly1305's `zeroize`
  feature, so key copies are still wiped when dropped. openmls still uses chacha20poly1305
  0.10, so both lines are in the build until it moves.
- **Patch and minor updates** (#379): tokio 1.54.1, uuid 1.29.1, libc 0.2.191, openmls 0.9.2,
  rustc-demangle 0.1.28 and rustls-native-certs 0.8.5; toml 1.2.1 (#392).

### Docs and spec

- **JEP-0013, Crypto Agility and a Post-Quantum Path** (Draft) is in the spec (#322).
- **JEP-0016, Useful Work and Auditors** (Draft) is in the spec (#366).
- **New contributor docs** (#321): `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/OWNERSHIP.md`, `docs/GOOD_FIRST_CONTRIBUTIONS.md`, and `scripts/dev-setup.sh` to set up a checkout.
- **The team's own deployment docs have left the public tree** (#323). `deploy/README.md` now
  covers any server behind a private network, and the channel-tier guide is in the README
  Quickstart.
- **The alpha.3 notes list the install.sh limitation** they shipped without (#369).

### Known limitations

- **Stop jig-server before re-running install.sh to upgrade.** The installer replaces the
  binaries but leaves a running server on the old build. Stop it first with
  `kill $(cat ~/.jig/jig-server.pid)` (or `$JIG_HOME/jig-server.pid` if you set `JIG_HOME`),
  then install (#334).
- **`jig channel join` from a follower is refused for a plaintext carried channel**
  (`CARRIED_CHANNEL`): it goes to the follower's membership endpoint, which does not relay to
  the owner. Join on the owner's server for now (#396).
- **A shared channel whose slug matches one of the follower's own channels** cannot be used by
  its slug from a client on that follower: the slug reads the follower's own channel, with no
  error. Name the shared channel by its id instead (#388).
- **A shared channel that stalled before this release stays stalled**; see above.
- **Adding someone from another server to an encrypted channel** needs one of their key
  packages on the owner's server. Until they have run `jig` against it once (for example
  `jig --server <owner-url> channel list`), the add is refused with `NO_KEY_PACKAGE`.
- **In an encrypted channel, messages sent before you joined** show as
  `[cannot decrypt: …]`, not as sent before you joined.

### Threat-register entries mitigated

Statuses are as of this release. *Partial* means part of the entry's decision is implemented;
the register says which part.

| Entry | What this release does | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OP-09 Federation abuse | A peer's relayed post into a channel this server orders is refused, so the legacy relay can no longer write into a server's own channels (#398) | Partial |

Still open or accepted in this release, among others: OP-04 (metadata), OP-10 and AB-05 (Sybil
resistance), AB-06 (provable abuse in encrypted channels), and NS-03. The register lists them all.
